title: First Draft: ‘Excruciating’: Trump Allies React to White House Press Secretary’s First Day – As Her Claim to Be an Attorney Collapses
author: Martin Pengelly
content:
_On this day in 1964, civil rights campaigner Rev. Martin Luther King Jr. won
the Nobel Peace Prize. Just 35, he was then the youngest person ever given the
honor. Donald Trump is now 80 and has still not been awarded the prize he so
desperately and openly craves._

Good morning. **Martin** and **Swin** here, writing up another utterly bizarre
day in **Donald Trump 's** DC. Martin at least is old enough to have already
been quite old 10 years ago, when **Sean Spicer** kicked off the world of
weird that is Trump press secretaries, their press conferences, and their
relationships with both reporters and the basic concept of truth. There have
been some [doozies](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2021/nov/22/kayleigh-
mcenany-book-trump-press-secretary), but it seems that under new pick **Katie
Zacharia** , things are about to get stranger still.

In today's '**First Draft** ,' we take a look at Zacharia's terrible, no good,
absolutely horrible first press briefing and the gathering fallout from it. We
also consider new steps in Trump's shamelessly political investigation of
**Ilhan Omar** , and take in developments in the illegal Iran War and on the
midterms trail. In and on we go.

Speaking to reporters before leaving the White House for Alaska, Donald Trump
said he thought his new press secretary, ex-Fox talking head and [ardent hate,
conspiracy, and extremism
monger](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/12/politics/kfile-katie-zacharia-deleted-
tweets) Katie Zacharia, was **" very good"** in her first briefing, which
concluded not long before.

Safe to say, few reporters or pundits shared the president's confidence. In
barely 15 minutes at the briefing room podium, Zacharia read extremely
haltingly from notes, head down, then took very few questions, calling only on
right-wing sources: Breitbart, Fox, and the _Daily Mail_.

She failed to give an answer on whether the U.S. was still sharing
intelligence with Ukraine.** "I'll have to get back to you on that,"** she
said. A softball about doing her job as a mother of four produced a flub,
referring to** "My president, excuse me, my husband. That's a good one."**
That at least raised a laugh. Another question produced hard news, Zacharia
saying, **" We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign,"** meaning envoy to
Greece (and former Donald Trump Jr. fiancee) Kimberly Guilfoyle, who has been
caught up in corruption allegations. That made an impact, but Zacharia blurted
on for a bit about learning about work-life balance from predecessor Karoline
Leavitt, voice shaking all the while, and then was outta there pronto.

It wasn't just pundits who piled onto the airwaves to voice their
astonishment. **Swin** admits he had not realized Zacharia was taking her bow,
what with having been buried in projects including [a lengthy profile of White
House Wormtongue Stephen Miller](https://zeteo.com/p/stephen-miller-trump-
running-world).

Getting very annoyed at the sound of his phone constantly dinging, **Swin**
finally took a swift look. Republican operatives, Trump advisers, and
administration officials were blowing up the phone, panning Zacharia's
performance.
